_comment: The jsDelivr identifier: the harness turns the CDN lookup off unless a fixture asks for it (options), and answers the lookup from the fixture's network map. lib/undeclared.min.js is minified and declared NOWHERE - no VENDOR entry, no hash-DB match - so it would be rejected as unreviewable first-party code. The content-addressed lookup recognises it by its sha256 as a published release of a widely-used package, so it is identified and reported by find-lib-on-cdn (info) with the CDN URL its bytes came from: the developer is asked to declare it, not punished for it. Popularity still decides - the npm downloads answer is what makes this a library rather than an unknown blob (see the not-popular path in not-popular-vendor-source).
